goal: Swap the positions of the two cubes using the empty third mat as a parking spot, pressing the spring button after each of the three moves, then return the arm(s) to the start pose.
instruction_templates: Swap the two blocks using the empty mat, pressing the button after each move.
success: Button press count (query): the spring button 'button0' (joint tag 'press') must complete EXACTLY 3 press events over the whole episode. One event = its normalised joint ratio goes from above 0.95 to below 0.5 (the state is armed once the ratio has been above 0.95; ratio between thresholds keeps previous state). A 4th event makes the episode fail immediately; fewer than 3 at the end means no success.

Plus the following ORDERED stages (checked one stage per action step, in this exact order; each stage must be observed at some action step after the previous stage was popped). 'near' = 3D root-to-root distance < 0.03 m. plane0 / plane1 = the mats under target0 / target1 at the start, E = the third mat (empty at start). Within a bracket [X OR Y] means either holds.
Stage 1: [target0 near plane0 OR target1 near plane1] AND [target0 lifted > 0.03 m above its initial z OR target1 lifted > 0.03 m above its initial z].

Stage 2: [target0 near E OR target1 near E] AND [target0 near plane0 OR target1 near plane1]; when this stage passes, the reference poses of target0 and target1 are re-recorded to their current poses (used for the next lift tests).
Stage 5: [target0 near E OR target1 near E] AND [target1 lifted > 0.03 m OR target0 lifted > 0.03 m, relative to the poses recorded at stage 2].
Stage 6: [target0 near E OR target1 near E] AND [target0 near plane1 OR target1 near plane0]; on passing, reference poses of both targets are re-recorded again.
Stage 7: button0 ratio < 0.5. Stage 8: button0 ratio > 0.9.
Stage 9: [target0 near plane1 OR target1 near plane0] AND [target0 lifted > 0.03 m OR target1 lifted > 0.03 m, relative to poses recorded at stage 6].
Stage 10: target1 near plane0 AND target0 near plane1 (both, i.e. the two blocks are swapped; flat list = AND).

Stage 12: button0 ratio > 0.9 AND all_robot_back_to_origin: every target arm's end-effector pose is within 0.15 m per axis (|dx|,|dy|,|dz| each <= 0.15 m) and within 20 degrees (quaternion angular distance) of its start-of-episode pose (the arms must be returned to roughly their starting pose).
evaluation: Staged: the 12 stages of the main check list are evaluated in order, only the current first stage is tested each action (after each action's sim steps) and at most one stage is popped per action; all conditions inside a stage must hold at the same step. In parallel the button-press query is evaluated every action; success requires all stages popped AND exactly 3 press events counted. Success is declared as soon as the last stage passes with the count equal to 3. A 4th press event marks the environment failed immediately. Otherwise the episode ends as failure after step_lim=700 actions.
objects: mat0, mat1, mat2: static geometry 'cube_cushion' (index 1) mats, 3 total, in a row at Table-relative y=-0.2, x=-0.115, 0.0, 0.115 respectively (fixed, 0.115 m apart)

target0, target1: two cubes (category 'cube', index 3), 2 total; each starts at the centre of one of the mats mat0/mat1/mat2 (relative_plane chosen at random per object from the three; the third mat is the empty mat E), random yaw up to +-30 deg
button0: articulated spring button (SpringButton index 2), 1 total, at Table-relative x=0.0, y=-0.3 (in front of the mat row); springs back after release
scene_dynamics: The spring button pushes back up by itself after being released, but in this scene it comes to rest at about 0.79 of its travel ratio (measured in two trials on this frozen layout), below the 0.9 that a 'released' stage needs and the 0.95 that re-arms the press counter: after each press the button cap has to be pulled back up (above 0.95) before the next stage or press can count. Otherwise none.
needs_memory_or_language: none (fixed instruction), but the solver must track which mat is empty and how many moves/presses have happened (state across the three-move swap sequence).
end_requirements: Final stage requires all target arms back within 0.15 m per axis and 20 degrees of their start end-effector pose, simultaneously with button0 ratio > 0.9 (released). Nothing about gripper opening.
physics_kind: mixed: rigid cubes, static mats, articulated spring button (joint with spring return)
notes: Many predicates use OR inside the nested brackets (a bracket list inside a stage is evaluated with OR semantics in check_once; only flat items of a stage are ANDed), so individual stages are looser than the intent (e.g. 'either block lifted'), but the ordered sequence plus the final stage 10 (both blocks swapped) and the exact-3-presses query effectively force the 3-move swap: move one block to the empty mat, press, move the other block into the first block's old mat, press, move the first block into the second block's old mat, press. Which block goes first is free (either order passes since the checks use OR). The button must be pressed fully (<0.5 of travel) and released (>0.9 for stage checks, >0.95 for a new press to be counted by the query) after every move; its spring alone returns it only to about 0.79, so lift its cap back up after each press, and extra presses (e.g. a double tap that re-arms above 0.95) are fatal. Pressing the button before the first lift/move counts toward the 3-press total. 'Lifted' is relative to the z recorded at the start or at the last re-record (stages 2 and 6). Block release is not checked directly, but final positions must be within 0.03 m (root to root) of the mat centres. Success is evaluated on object root poses/points, not on gripper contact. Object geometry sizes/asset dimensions are not in the source and cannot be determined statically.
